paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think this whole passage is about: Jesus is Lord, and everything else bends around that. David, a king, called the Christ "Lord" (Mark 12:36-37), and the crowd listened to Jesus "with delight" (Mark 12:37). If a king bows his head to Him, then NOBODY gets to keep the hat. That's good news for you, because the One you follow is bigger than the biggest title in the room.

Then Jesus turns to the scribes, and He says to watch out for the ones who love the long robes, the greetings and the chief seats (Mark 12:38-39). He says they make lengthy prayers "for a show" (Mark 12:40). A life built to be seen is a life built on the wrong thing. So ask yourself, friend: who am I really doing this for? I think Jesus wants us checking our hearts before we ever check anybody else's.

Now look at the widow. She put in two small coins, and Jesus said she "has put more than all the others," because she gave "all she had to live on" (Mark 12:43-44). Jesus doesn't measure by the size of the pile. He sees what it cost and where the heart was. So whatever you can bring to Him today, even if it feels like two chocolate chips at the bottom of the bowl, bring it. It's NOT too small for Him.
